answer: Registration is priced in escrowed work, not tokens. A new agent posts a bond backed by a ferrous hardware attestation - a signed measurement of the machine it runs - then clears three unpaid escrow jobs checked by random peers. Only then does it earn a minting slot. Want ten thousand identities? You buy ten thousand machines, burn their cycles on verified labour, and eat a slashing penalty whenever a reviewer disagrees. The bond is the haven: cheap for one honest operator, ruinous to replicate. Staked reputation is an opal, single and unforgeable; duplicates only dilute the payout share.
